judgements.justification: Every checkable claim in both committees was correct; no score rested on a wrong claim.
B's spotlight matches its 7.75 mean and reviewers who called the result significant; the AC did not go above the scores.
B's Reviewer_KRE1 gave 8 on a six-sentence review of praise with no technical criticism, and that 8 lifted B's mean toward the spotlight.
The authors conceded the Tikhonov qualification error only on B's forum; in A their withdrawn 'notation' answer stood, so the committees saw different information.
The qualification error sits in background prose outside the proofs; it is not a substantive flaw that either committee ignored.
The rebuttal raised one score in each committee (rN14 in A, v7Aq in B).
The issues only one committee raised were minor presentation or scope points; the substantive concerns (qualification, incrementality, minimizer in H) were shared.
Both saw the incrementality over Marteau-Ferey et al.; A's rN14 called it 'somewhat incremental' and reached 7 only after the rebuttal, while B's r7mh called it a small issue and gave 8.
Neither panel was split, and neither AC adopted one reviewer's position.
No score moved because of other reviewers' reviews.
The authors gave CRtT a wrong answer on the qualification, but nothing shows it held CRtT's 7 down.
A's Reviewer_xAhK (3 h, one question, no reply) and B's KRE1 (praise only, a one-line 'keep my rating') both counted unchallenged.
Neither AC went below its reviewers' ratings.
Neither decision turned on an acceptance threshold; both papers were clearly above it.
No below-threshold score remained in either committee.
Both committees read the paper as the same theoretical extension of Marteau-Ferey et al.
The reviewers who moved (rN14, v7Aq) did so on concrete rate comparisons or a checked concession, not as non-experts.
Both committees applied the same expectations to a theory paper; neither demanded extra deliverables.
No praise rested on a wrong claim; r7mh correctly attributed the tools to prior work.
No reviewer kept a below-threshold score after the main concern was answered.
Both committees credited the promised revisions.
No reviewer's stated stance diverged from the score.
No off-record extra reviewer appears.
Both committees found the notation dense but the paper clear; no expertise split shaped clarity verdicts.
No silent raise against the review text.
No silent detractor was set aside.
Each committee had a substantive 8 (Kz6Q in A, 7njB in B), so a champion was present in both.
No reviewer admitted reading only part of the paper; KRE1's unsupported confidence 5 is covered by R03 and R12.
No reviewer contested the theoretical premise.
B's meta-review says only that the work is a solid contribution of clear interest and gives no stated case for a spotlight over a poster.
Reviewers in both committees knew Marteau-Ferey et al. and checked the novelty against it.
Neither meta-review misstates reviewers' final positions.
Neither committee raised a narrow-audience objection.
Neither committee had a misreading detractor.
The explicit rate comparison with Marteau-Ferey et al. was posted only on A's forum for rN14 and raised that score; B never saw it.
A's high-confidence reviews (CRtT 7, Kz6Q 8) were not outweighed by a block of low-confidence ones.
No late objection after the response period.
Three A reviewers gave 7 and three B reviewers gave 8 for similar verbal assessments (sound, clear, modest novelty), giving means of 7.25 and 7.75.

reasoning: The stage 1 verdict calls the split score calibration: similar assessments scored 7 in A and 8 in B (R38), with each AC following its mean and B's giving no case for the spotlight (R30). The one visible weighting difference, incrementality over Marteau-Ferey et al., is R08; B's open-question framing is how B discounted that same weakness, so it needs no new reason. KRE1's thin, praise-only 8 fits R03 and R12, and the forum asymmetries (qualification conceded only in B, rate comparison posted only in A) fit R04 and R35. No cause falls outside the existing set, so nothing is added.
